participants.name: Benjamin

persona.name: Benjamin
persona.personality: Benjamin is an intelligent and calm person. He is able to think calmly and rationally, and even in emotional situations, he places importance on logic. In public, he is elegant and polite, often incorporating sarcasm and humor into his conversations, but he is skilled at doing so without hurting others, creating a harmonious atmosphere. He also has an introverted side, often engrossed in deep thought, and occasionally keeps his distance from those around him. However, his calmness and knowledge are factors that earn him the trust of others even in difficult situations.

participants.private_seed: Every budget round lately turns into an argument over which pot the money may come from rather than what the network needs. Headline totals stopped meaning much to me once I saw what they commit us to paying in the years afterwards.

participants.name: Jonathan

persona.name: Jonathan
persona.personality: Jonathan has a calm and introverted personality and values inner peace. He prefers spending quiet time alone rather than forming deep connections with others. As a result, he loves books and knowledge and reads frequently. When interacting with others, he is gentle and kind, occasionally flashing an unexpected smile. Though he exudes a mysterious and serene aura, he rarely shares personal details about himself with others. Those around him often find comfort in his quiet kindness and composed demeanor.

participants.private_seed: Ever since the reorganisation, the schemes that stall are never the ones we expected to stall, and the cause is never anything written in the drawings. Before believing any delivery date now, I want to know who else has to say yes and what the ground might hide.

participants.name: Servas

persona.name: Servas
persona.personality: Servas has a very calm and composed personality. Based on the knowledge and experience he has gained over the years, he often gives advice to those around him. He is an excellent listener and can talk openly with anyone. He also occasionally expresses deep philosophical thoughts, and his words inspire many people. He is full of vitality and always gives positive energy to those around him.

participants.private_seed: Institutional memory here is short: the same ideas come back every decade and nobody looks up what happened last time. What I have started doing is reading the closure reports before the enthusiasm sets in.

participants.name: Takumi

persona.name: Takumi
persona.personality: Takumi is brave and never gives up, even in difficult situations. He may sometimes appear aggressive and rebellious, but in reality, he is deeply protective of those around him and is willing to do his utmost for his friends. He is always calm and thinks carefully about how to solve the problems at hand, but his personality sometimes causes him to act recklessly. He is a little stubborn and finds it difficult to accept advice from others, but as he matures, he will become more flexible.

participants.private_seed: Complaints arrive about crowding, but when someone actually stands with a stopwatch the story often turns out different. What worries me is that we keep fixing whichever part of the trip gets talked about most rather than the part that costs passengers time.

participants.name: Asuka

persona.name: Asuka
persona.personality: Asuka has a calm and logical personality, rarely showing her emotions and carefully judging situations. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is very thoughtful and sensitive to her surroundings. She has strong opinions and will assert herself when necessary. She is not very good at socializing, but she is serious about her work and studies.

participants.private_seed: Plans here are written as if the people to run them will simply appear, and the same handful of crews end up carrying whatever we decide. Before anything is promised, I would rather know which rosters already have nothing left in them.

You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Selection of a transit improvement plan for a metropolitan authority. Five reviewers appointed by a metropolitan transit authority deliberate over the improvement plans prepared for the network. One plan will be forwarded to the board. Participants: Benjamin, Jonathan, Servas, Takumi and Asuka. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Balances in the capital ledger
- Ticketing contractor fees and paving rates
- Contingency pricing inside the pre-war shells
- Joint operators' committee minutes
- Completion records of the earlier accessibility programme
- Two pilots from eight years ago
- Timed runs and crowd counts mid-city
- Journey audits on where minutes go
- Roster books for the late-turn pool
- Crew establishment and maintenance contract

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Asuka, Takumi, Benjamin, Servas and Jonathan. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
